name: Patti Smith
who_line: She wanted to look like a poet, not a girl singer. She did not have money. She had a picture of Baudelaire and a clean shirt.
who: Patti Smith came out of New York as a poet who also had a band. Horses (1975) is the record and the photograph: Robert Mapplethorpe, a Salvation Army men’s white shirt, cuffs cut off the one that recalled Brassaï’s Genet, a black jacket flung Sinatra-style. Arista wanted a bouffant and the lip hair airbrushed. She refused.

She found Rimbaud in a Philadelphia bus depot at sixteen because the cover looked like it glittered. She dressed like Baudelaire because she liked dressing like Baudelaire, not because she was thinking she would break boundaries. Later the black-and-white is Ann Demeulemeester, worn until it is sweat and holes.
work: Horses, Radio Ethiopia, Easter and “Because the Night” (written with Bruce Springsteen). Then a long quiet in Detroit, then the return. Since she began performing again after Ann mailed three white shirts from Antwerp, she has said she has never gone onstage without wearing a piece by Ann. They are talismanic.
The Horses shirt and Ann’s three white shirts are one friendship. Do not flatten her into a muse caption. She is the poet the house found in a record-shop window.

quotes.text: I had no sense of how it would look, just that it should be true. The only thing I think I promised Robert is that I would wear a clean shirt with no stains on it.

I thought of myself as a poet and a performer, and so how did I dress? I didn’t have much money; I liked to dress like Baudelaire. I looked at a picture of him and he was dressed, like, with this ribbon or tie and a white shirt. I wasn’t thinking that I was going to break any boundaries. I just like dressing like Baudelaire.

I derive great power from wearing Ann’s clothes. Since I began performing again, after that first gift, I have never gone onstage without wearing a piece by Ann… They make me feel confident, they make me feel truly like myself. They are talismanic.

I found him in a Philadelphia bus depot when I was sixteen. I remember seeing a copy of Illuminations for sale on a table of used books. Of course, illuminations is a great word, but what I was really taken by was the cover. It was a beautiful picture of Rimbaud. That’s why I got the book.

why_the_look: She wanted to look like a poet, not a girl singer. She did not have money. She had a picture of Baudelaire and a clean shirt.
beliefs: Rimbaud first (crush, then language). Genet via the Brassaï picture on the shirt. Baudelaire’s cravat. In Patti Smith Complete she also lists June Christy’s ponytail, a raincoat à la Camus, Dylan’s snap-tab collar, Ava Gardner’s black capris. To Rolling Stone, 1 January 1976, the same Rimbaud cover “looked so cool, just like Bob Dylan.”

moments.title: Horses cover — Mapplethorpe
moments.garments: Salvation Army men’s white shirts; cuffs cut off the one that recalled Brassaï’s Genet; RV monogram she liked to imagine as Roger Vadim. Black jacket flung Sinatra-style. No makeup.
moments.where_it_lives: The sleeve itself / Mapplethorpe estate. Do not hotlink the cover.
moments.why_iconic: Arista wanted a bouffant and the lip hair airbrushed. She refused. Mapplethorpe said this one has the magic. Smith: when I look at it now, I never see me. I see us.

media.caption: Rights-locked. The sleeve is the document. Do not hotlink.
